name: start.me
tagline: A customizable browser start page with bookmark widgets, RSS feeds, notes and shared team pages.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A start page is a grid of links, some RSS boxes, and a notes widget. None of that requires a company. An agent can build a drag-and-drop dashboard with bookmark groups, favicon fetching, feed reading and JSON import/export in one sitting, and if you self-host it behind a tiny server you get cross-device access too. The paid tiers mostly sell polish, browser integration and shared pages for teams, which is exactly the part a personal build skips without pain.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted start page serving draggable widget columns of bookmark groups, RSS feeds and sticky notes, backed by SQLite with JSON import/export.
requirements: a machine or cheap VPS to host it if you want it on more than one device
an export of your existing bookmarks (HTML or JSON)
whatYouLose: Browser extension and mobile apps, so setting it as the new tab page on phones is clumsy
Hosted sync with accounts, sharing and permissions across a team
Curated page templates and the widget gallery (weather, calendars, embeds) that ship working out of the box
Automatic dead link checking and bookmark import from every browser and service
Someone else keeping the RSS parsing and favicon fetching from quietly rotting
moatNotes: Once a few hundred links live in a paid start page, the export button is technically there but nobody ever presses it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a start page is the first thing you see all day and jank is intolerable there. start.me sells a thing that already looks right on every device, syncs without you thinking about it, and lets a team point at one shared page of resources. People also pay to stop maintaining it: the widget that breaks on a Tuesday is not your problem. A personal build wins on control and cost, and loses on the phone.
notes: The rare SaaS where the DIY version is arguably nicer, because your start page should reflect your taste, not a template gallery.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted personal start page called "Homebase". No accounts, no telemetry, no third-party SaaS.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Backend: Node 20 + Express + better-sqlite3, single file server.
- Frontend: Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind, built to static files that Express serves.
- Data: one SQLite file at ./data/homebase.db. Create it on first run.

Data model:
- widgets: id, column (0-2), position, type ('links' | 'feed' | 'note'), title, config JSON.
- links: id, widget_id, title, url, favicon_url, position.
- Feed widget config: feed URL, item count. Note widget config: markdown text.

Features in scope:
- Three-column responsive grid of widgets. Drag to reorder widgets between columns and links within a links widget. Use dnd-kit.
- Inline editing: add/rename/delete widgets, add/edit/delete links, edit note text as markdown with a simple renderer.
- Favicons: server endpoint that fetches https://icons.duckduckgo.com/ip3/DOMAIN.ico, caches the bytes in ./data/icons, and serves them locally. Never hotlink at render time.
- RSS/Atom: server endpoint fetches and parses feeds with rss-parser, caches results in SQLite for 15 minutes, returns title, link, date. The server does the fetching so CORS is not a problem.
- Import: accept a browser bookmarks HTML export and turn each top-level folder into a links widget.
- Export: GET /api/export returns the whole database as JSON. POST /api/import restores it.
- Keyboard: '/' focuses a search box that filters all links live and opens the top match on Enter.
- Dead link check: a manual button that HEAD-requests every link with a 5s timeout and flags failures in the UI. Do not run it automatically.
- Dark mode by default, light mode toggle, both readable.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, multi-user sharing, browser extension, weather or calendar widgets, mobile apps, any analytics.

Ops:
- .env holds PORT and optional BASIC_AUTH_USER / BASIC_AUTH_PASS; if both are set, wrap all routes in basic auth so it is safe to expose on a LAN or VPS. Ship .env.example, never real secrets.
- npm run dev for Vite + server, npm run build, npm start for production.
- Seed the database with three example widgets so the first load is not empty.
- README: setup, how to import bookmarks, how to set it as your browser new tab page, where the SQLite file lives, how to back it up.
